title: Chapter 14: Making of the Indian Constitution

blocks.content: The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the country. It lays down the framework of political principles, procedures, rights, duties and powers of government institutions. The making of the Constitution was a long historical process that involved many committees and debates.
1. Background of the Indian Constitution

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) laid the foundation for creating the Constituent Assembly.
The Constituent Assembly was entrusted with the historic responsibility of framing the Indian Constitution.
Multiple important committees were formed within the Assembly to oversee different sections of drafting.
The drafting process systematically shaped the fundamental features and principles of the Constitution.
The formal adoption of the Constitution established the legal framework of modern India.

blocks.content: • The demand for a constitution for India developed during the freedom movement.
• The British government gradually introduced constitutional reforms in India.
• Acts such as the Government of India Act 1919 and Government of India Act 1935 influenced the constitution.
2. Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)
• The British government sent the Cabinet Mission to India in 1946.
• The mission proposed the formation of a Constituent Assembly.
• The members of the assembly were elected indirectly by provincial legislatures.
3. Constituent Assembly
4. Important Committees of the Constituent Assembly
Making of the Indian Constitution
5. Drafting of the Constitution
• The Drafting Committee was formed on 29 August 1947.
• It was responsible for preparing the draft constitution.
• The committee studied constitutions of many countries.
6. Adoption of the Constitution
• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
• It came into force on 26 January 1950.
• This day is celebrated as Republic Day.
7. Features of the Indian Constitution
• Longest written constitution in the world.
• Federal system with unitary features.
• Parliamentary form of government.
• Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.
• Independent judiciary.

items: The year and significance of the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) are frequently tested in competitive exams.
Questions often cover the roles and heads of Important Committees of the Constituent Assembly.
Understand the key milestones leading from drafting to final adoption of the Indian Constitution.

• Indian Constitution influenced by Government of India Act 1935.
